title: Theorem on formal functions over a Noetherian affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to f^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] (the ideal sheaf generated by the images of the elements of $I$), and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], with $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). Fix $p\ge0$ and put $H=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], an $A$-module, and $H^\wedge=\varprojlim_nH/I^nH$ its $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The quotient maps $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ induce $A$-linear maps $H\to H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$, which vanish on $I^nH$ (as $I^n$ acts on $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ through $\mathcal I^n$, which kills it) and so induce maps $\theta_n:H/I^nH\to H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ compatible with the transition maps on both sides. Then $\varprojlim_n\theta_n:H^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. In particular ($p=0$) the maps $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)/I^n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ induce an isomorphism $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)^\wedge\cong\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648) and its proof, which uses Lemma 02OB (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal, line 5553: the Mittag-Leffler property and the Artin-Rees type bound); the 'homeomorphism for the limit topologies' clause of 02OC is not stated here

proof.text: (Module structures and the maps $\theta_n$.) For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, $a\in A$ acts on $H^p(X,\mathcal G)$ as $H^p$ of multiplication by the image $f^\sharp(a)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$; since $H^p(X,-)$ is an additive functor [pqf-def-cohomology], every map induced by an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map is $A$-linear. Put $M_n=H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ ($n\ge1$), let $\rho_n:H\to M_n$ be induced by $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ and $\tau_{k,n}:M_k\to M_n$ ($k\ge n$) by $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^k\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$; by functoriality $\tau_{k,n}\rho_k=\rho_n$, $\tau_{n,n}=1$ and $\tau_{l,n}=\tau_{k,n}\tau_{l,k}$. If $a\in I^n$, write $a=\sum_j a_{j1}\cdots a_{jn}$ with $a_{ji}\in I$; each $f^\sharp(a_{ji})$ is a global section of $\mathcal I$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], so $f^\sharp(a)$ is a section of $\mathcal I^n$ and multiplication by it maps $\mathcal F$ into $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), i.e. is $0$ on $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$. Hence $I^nM_n=0$, so $\rho_n(I^nH)=I^n\rho_n(H)=0$ and $\rho_n$ factors through $\theta_n:H/I^nH\to M_n$; the $\theta_n$ are compatible with the transition maps because $\tau_{k,n}\rho_k=\rho_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: (The constant $c$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-ml-cohomology-powers-ideal] for $A,I,f,\mathcal F,p$ (same hypotheses) there is $c\ge0$ with (1) $K_n:=\operatorname{Ker}(\rho_n)\subseteq I^{n-c}H$ for $n\ge\max(c,1)$, and (2) $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})=N_n:=\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$ for $n\ge1$, $k\ge n+c$. Note $N_n\subseteq M_n$ and $\tau_{k,n}(N_k)=\tau_{k,n}\rho_k(H)=\rho_n(H)=N_n$, so $(N_n)$ is an inverse subsystem of $(M_n)$ with surjective transition maps.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: ($\varprojlim N_n=\varprojlim M_n$; Stacks: 'it follows that $\lim M_n=\lim N_n$'.) The inclusion of systems $(N_n)\subseteq(M_n)$ induces an injective $A$-linear map $\varprojlim_nN_n\to\varprojlim_nM_n$ (both are submodules of $\prod_nM_n$). It is surjective: if $(x_n)_n\in\varprojlim M_n$, then for each $n$, $x_n=\tau_{n+c,n}(x_{n+c})\in\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{n+c,n})=N_n$ by step 2, so $(x_n)_n\in\varprojlim N_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: ($\varprojlim N_n=\varprojlim H/K_n$.) $\rho_n$ induces $A$-linear isomorphisms $\bar\rho_n:H/K_n\to N_n$; since $\tau_{k,n}\rho_k=\rho_n$ we have $K_k\subseteq K_n$ for $k\ge n$, and the $\bar\rho_n$ commute with the transition maps $H/K_k\to H/K_n$ and $\tau_{k,n}|_{N_k}$. So $\varprojlim\bar\rho_n:\varprojlim_nH/K_n\to\varprojlim_nN_n$ is an isomorphism (inverse $\varprojlim\bar\rho_n^{-1}$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: (The two filtrations agree; Stacks: '$K_n\subset I^{n-c}M$ ... $I^nM\subset K_n$'.) For $n\ge1$, $I^nH\subseteq K_n$ by step 1 ($\rho_n(I^nH)=0$); for $n\ge1$, $K_{n+c}\subseteq I^nH$ by step 2 (1) applied to $n+c\ge\max(c,1)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: ($\varprojlim H/I^nH=\varprojlim H/K_n$.) By step 5 the quotient maps $\pi_n:H/I^nH\to H/K_n$ and $\sigma_n:H/K_{n+c}\to H/I^nH$ are defined, $A$-linear, and compatible with the transition maps (all are induced by $\mathrm{id}_H$). Moreover $\sigma_n\pi_{n+c}$ is the transition map $H/I^{n+c}H\to H/I^nH$ and $\pi_n\sigma_n$ is the transition map $H/K_{n+c}\to H/K_n$. Let $\pi=\varprojlim\pi_n:H^\wedge\to\varprojlim H/K_n$ and $\sigma:\varprojlim H/K_n\to H^\wedge$, $(y_n)_n\mapsto(\sigma_n(y_{n+c}))_n$ (compatible since the $\sigma_n$ are). For $(x_n)\in H^\wedge$, $\sigma\pi(x)=(\sigma_n\pi_{n+c}(x_{n+c}))_n=(x_n)_n$, and for $(y_n)\in\varprojlim H/K_n$, $\pi\sigma(y)=(\pi_n\sigma_n(y_{n+c}))_n=(y_n)_n$. Hence $\pi$ is an $A$-linear isomorphism; here $H^\wedge=\varprojlim_nH/I^nH$ as in the statement [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), proof (lines 5673-5702)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The composite $H^\wedge\xrightarrow{\pi}\varprojlim H/K_n\xrightarrow{\varprojlim\bar\rho_n}\varprojlim N_n\subseteq\varprojlim M_n$ is an isomorphism by steps 3, 4 and 6. On components it sends $(x_n\bmod I^nH)_n$ to $(\rho_n(x_n))_n=(\theta_n(x_n\bmod I^nH))_n$, so it equals $\varprojlim_n\theta_n$, which is therefore an isomorphism of $A$-modules. For $p=0$, $H^0(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], giving the last assertion.
